questions.q: What problem do sharing rules solve that the role hierarchy structurally can't, per this lesson?
options: Sharing rules restrict access below OWD
Sharing rules extend access to groups of users who aren't related by the hierarchy -- peers or cross-functional teams
Sharing rules replace the need for profiles entirely
Sharing rules control field-level security instead of record access
questions.explain: The role hierarchy only opens access upward along reporting lines; sharing rules reach peers and cross-functional groups it can't.

questions.q: What's the difference between an owner-based and a criteria-based sharing rule?
options: Owner-based shares by who owns the record; criteria-based shares by field values regardless of owner
Owner-based only works on custom objects; criteria-based only works on standard objects
They are two names for the same mechanism
Criteria-based rules can only target individual users
questions.explain: Owner-based rules key off record ownership; criteria-based rules key off field values on the record, with no ownership check.

questions.q: Who can be the recipient of a sharing rule?
options: A public group, a role, or a role and its subordinates -- never an individual user directly
Only an individual named user
Only the System Administrator profile
Only another sharing rule
questions.explain: The lesson states sharing rules always target a public group, a role, or a role and its subordinates, never an individual directly.

questions.q: An object's OWD is already Public Read/Write internally. What does adding a sharing rule to that object accomplish, per this lesson?
options: It narrows access back down for specific users
Nothing meaningful -- sharing rules only add access, and there's nothing left to add above Public Read/Write
It overrides the OWD setting entirely
It automatically converts the object's OWD to Private
questions.explain: Sharing rules only widen access on top of OWD; an object already fully open at OWD has nothing left for a sharing rule to add.

questions.q: Where do sharing rules sit in the record-access stack relative to the role hierarchy, per this lesson?
options: Below OWD, as the very first check applied
Above the automatic role hierarchy, opening access sideways and across by explicit configuration
They replace the role hierarchy entirely in modern Salesforce orgs
They apply only after manual sharing has been configured
questions.explain: The stack diagram places sharing rules above the automatic role hierarchy layer, extending access to explicitly configured groups.
